ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure is a 4×4 grid, with each small square being a unit square. The shaded figure is enclosed by several line segments, and all endpoints lie on grid points. Taking the lower-left corner as (0,0) and the upper-right corner as (4,4), the vertices can be read in order along the outer boundary of the shading from the figure as: (2,4), (1,2), (2,2), (0,0), (2,1), (4,0), (3,2), (4,4), (2,3), then back to (2,4). Reasoning: Use the shoelace formula to calculate the area of this grid-point polygon. The forward sum is 2·2 + 1·2 + 2·0 + 0·1 + 2·0 + 4·2 + 3·4 + 4·3 + 2·4 = 46. The reverse sum is 4·1 + 2·2 + 2·0 + 0·2 + 1·4 + 0·3 + 2·4 + 4·2 + 3·2 = 34. Area = |46 - 34| / 2 = 6. Because the area of each small square is 1, the area of the shaded region is 6.

method.method_draft: Coordinate/shoelace route. First read the image as a 4-by-4 square grid with the shaded symbol bounded by straight segments whose endpoints lie on grid intersections. Assign coordinates to the grid intersections, for example using the lower-left corner as (0,0) and the upper-right corner as (4,4). Trace the outer boundary of the shaded region, splitting it into simple lattice polygons if the concave middle parts make one outline inconvenient. For each simple polygon, apply the shoelace formula using the coordinates read from the grid; add the resulting polygon areas. Because the text says each small square is a unit square, the coordinate area is already in square units, giving total shaded area 6.

method.method_draft: Unit-square fraction/complement route. First read the image as a 4-by-4 unit grid and inspect each of the 16 small squares. Mark which parts are shaded: several cells are fully shaded, while the remaining shaded or unshaded pieces are right triangles or trapezoids cut by the visible diagonals between grid intersections. Instead of using coordinates, pair congruent triangular pieces across neighboring cells to form whole unit squares, and combine any full shaded cells directly. Equivalently, count the unshaded whole-square and half-square pieces inside the 16-unit grid and subtract from 16. The paired pieces show that the shaded region covers 6 unit squares in total.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：The image shows a 4-by-4 grid, so there are 16 unit squares total. A gray shaded polygon runs through the grid with slanted edges connecting grid points. Two middle squares in the shaded band are completely shaded, and the other shaded portions are triangular or trapezoidal pieces cut off by the diagonals.

推理：The total grid area is 16. Using the unit-square pairing/complement idea, the partial shaded pieces can be paired across neighboring cells to form whole unit-square areas. There are 2 fully shaded unit squares in the middle. The remaining slanted shaded pieces group into 4 more unit squares of area. Thus the shaded area is 2 + 4 = 6. Equivalently, the unshaded complement totals 10 unit squares, so 16 - 10 = 6.
